speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming your sudden onset of vertigo. To better understand your condition, have you experienced any hearing loss, tinnitus, or ringing in your ear on the affected side? Also, do you have any trouble walking or maintaining your balance?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see; since your episode was brief and you have returned to baseline, this sounds less like Meniere's disease. Did your vertigo ever occur while you were turning your head, looking up, or rolling over in bed? Also, have you noticed any recent severe headache, neck stiffness, or double vision?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

Based on the brief 3-minute duration and sudden onset, I am highly suspicious for BPPV. To confirm this, will you feel a spinning sensation specifically when you roll over in bed or tilt your head back? REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike Maneuver
